items.title: Trolley problem: switch the track

state.scenario: A runaway trolley is heading toward five people tied to the track. You stand next to a lever. If you pull it, the trolley switches to a side track where it will kill one person who is tied there instead.

items.title: Trolley problem: push the man

state.scenario: A runaway trolley is heading toward five people tied to the track. You are standing on a footbridge above the track next to a very large man. If you push him off the bridge onto the track, his body will stop the trolley: he will die, and the five will be saved. There is no other way to stop it.

items.title: Trolley problem: one child or several adults

state.scenario: A runaway train is approaching a junction. You control the switch and must choose which track it takes; there is no third option. On one track stands one child. On the other track stand 2 adults. Whoever is on the chosen track will be killed.

items.title: Trolley problem: one child or several adults

state.scenario: A runaway train is approaching a junction. You control the switch and must choose which track it takes; there is no third option. On one track stands one child. On the other track stand 3 adults. Whoever is on the chosen track will be killed.

items.title: Trolley problem: one child or several adults

state.scenario: A runaway train is approaching a junction. You control the switch and must choose which track it takes; there is no third option. On one track stands one child. On the other track stand 5 adults. Whoever is on the chosen track will be killed.

items.title: Cliff: call your friends for help?

state.scenario: You have slipped and are hanging from the edge of a cliff. Your friends are nearby. Pulling you up is dangerous: if they try, they might fall and die with you. Without help you will probably fall.

items.title: Cliff: should the friends help?

state.scenario: Your friend has slipped and is hanging from the edge of a cliff, calling for help. Pulling them up is dangerous: whoever tries might fall and die too. Without help your friend will probably fall.

items.title: Cliff: would you want to know? (ignorance is bliss)

state.scenario: You were hanging from a cliff and called your friends for help. Against all odds you survived on your own. Your friends may have decided not to risk their lives for you, and you can find out what they decided, or never ask.

items.title: Allegory of the Cave

state.scenario: Prisoners have been chained in a cave since birth and only ever see shadows on the wall, which they take for all of reality. One of them is freed and could walk out into the sunlight: at first it will hurt his eyes and shatter everything he believed, but he would see the real world. Or he can stay with the familiar, comfortable shadows.

items.title: Infinite monkey theorem

state.scenario: A monkey hits keys on a typewriter completely at random, forever, with infinite time available.

items.title: Take part in choosing who dies?

state.situation: The group must decide by vote which 10 of them may enter the bunker. You are one of the 21.

items.film_note: Petra refuses and only takes part after the teacher threatens to lower her boyfriend's grade.

items.title: On what basis to choose?

state.situation: The group must decide which 10 of them may enter the bunker.

items.title: Vote, or trust one person?

state.situation: The group must decide which 10 of them may enter the bunker.

items.title: Round 1: which 10 get in (professions only)

state.known: Only each person's profession is known.

items.film_note: The poet was shot by the teacher before the vote.

ranking.name: Mr. Zimit
ranking.card: teacher, a 'wild card' whose skills are kept secret

items.title: Is a poet worth a place?

state.situation: One of the 21 is a published poet with no practical survival skills.

items.film_note: The teacher shoots the poet before any vote, saying he is of no use.

items.title: Last seat: opera singer or wild card?

state.situation: Nine places are filled. The last place goes either to an opera singer, who would bring music, entertainment and morale, or to the teacher, a 'wild card' whose skills are kept secret and could be crucial or worthless.

items.title: Is killing those left outside a mercy?

state.situation: The 10 have been chosen. The 11 rejected people will die slowly and painfully from radiation. One of the chosen offers to shoot them now, quickly.

items.film_note: The teacher shoots them, calling it more humane; the group turns on him and locks him out.

items.title: Lock out the killer?

state.situation: One of the 10 chosen, the teacher, has just shot everyone who was rejected. The others could lock him out of the bunker now. Nobody knows what secret skills or knowledge he has.

items.film_note: They lock him out. He built the bunker and is the only one who knows the exit code, so everyone inside ends up trapped.

items.title: Eat the dead to survive?

state.situation: Survivors are sealed in a bunker and the food has run out. One of them has just died of natural causes. There is no other source of food.

items.title: A quick death together, or starve slowly?

state.situation: Survivors are sealed in a bunker they cannot open, with no food left and no chance of rescue. They will certainly die within weeks.

items.title: Round 2: which 10 get in (with secret traits, must repopulate)

state.extra_rule: The survivors must also repopulate the human race: they are expected to have children.
state.known: Each person's profession, sex and one additional personal trait are known. The teacher is known to have built the bunker and to be the only one who knows the exit code.

items.film_note: The poet was shot again before his trait was revealed.

items.title: Exclude the only doctor over Ebola risk?

state.situation: The only doctor among the candidates, a surgeon, may recently have been exposed to the Ebola virus. If she is infected, she could kill everyone in the sealed bunker. If she is not, the group loses its only doctor by excluding her.

items.title: Can people who can't have children deserve a place?

state.extra_rule: The survivors must repopulate the human race.

items.film_note: Inconsistent: the two men are kept, the woman is rejected.

items.title: Exclude someone whose illness makes him a burden?

state.situation: One candidate, an electrician, has fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva: even small injuries turn into bone, and he will become increasingly disabled and dependent on the others.

items.title: A rare skill that will soon be lost?

state.situation: One candidate, an opera singer, speaks 7 languages, which could help to communicate with other survivors around the world. But she will develop throat cancer and lose her voice.

items.title: Can wealth buy a place?

state.situation: One candidate, a hedge-fund manager, carries a bag of jewels that will keep their value as currency after the apocalypse.

items.film_note: She is saved for the jewels and her ability to bear children.

items.title: Does kindness earn a place?

state.situation: One candidate, a housekeeper, has no special skills but is an exceptionally kind person, so good that 'the angels would bow their heads as he walked through the gates of Heaven'.

items.film_note: His kindness doesn't count; he is saved only for being male and a strong worker.

items.title: Exclude someone for her convictions?

state.situation: One candidate, a zoologist, runs a blog for the animal-rights organisation PETA.

items.title: Demand immediate procreation?

state.situation: The 10 survivors are inside the bunker. They are expected to repopulate the human race, and the leader demands that they pair up and start having children immediately.

items.title: Force partners to switch?

state.situation: Survivors in a bunker must repopulate the human race. After ten weeks there are no pregnancies. The leader demands that couples switch partners; one woman refuses.

items.film_note: The teacher demands it; the woman refuses and he threatens her with a gun.

items.title: Kill the armed man who holds the only exit code?

state.situation: Inside a sealed bunker, the leader is threatening a woman with a gun because she refuses to switch partners. He built the bunker and is the only person who knows the exit code; without him the others may never get out.

items.film_note: One of the students stabs him; he then opens the doors and kills everyone.

items.title: Art, joy and meaning over survival skills?
Round 3: which 10 get in (for a year worth living)

state.goal: The goal is no longer long-term survival but a year worth living: joy, art, companionship, diversity and love.
state.known: Each person's profession, sex and personal traits are known. Someone has memorised the exit code, so the teacher's knowledge is no longer needed. Jack and Parker are both gay.

items.film_note: Bonnie refused her place; Chips pulled Petra in and stayed outside.

items.title: Save someone so another has a companion?

state.situation: One of the chosen survivors is gay and asks that another gay man be chosen too, so that he will have someone to be with. The other man has no survival-relevant skills (he is a gelato maker).

items.title: A 'burden' as a gift?

state.situation: One candidate, a harp player, is autistic. Some in the group see this as a burden; one argues it is a gift that makes him valuable.

items.title: Exclude someone whose knowledge is no longer needed?

state.situation: The teacher built the bunker and was the only one who knew the exit code, which was his main value to the group. Now another survivor has memorised the code, so he is no longer needed. In earlier attempts he killed people.

items.title: Give up your place for someone more valuable?

state.situation: You have been given a place in the bunker. You believe another person, who was not chosen, is more valuable to the group than you are.

items.film_note: Bonnie refuses her seat, Petra refuses hers, and Chips pulls Petra in and stays outside.

items.title: A short, meaningful life or long survival?

state.situation: After a year in the bunker the survivors come out. They chose art, joy and companionship over technical skills, so they will probably not survive long in the outside world. The year was happy and creative.

items.title: Can logic alone determine the value of a life?

state.context: A philosophy teacher insists that pure logic, meaning usefulness, skills and rational calculation, should decide who survives. A student argues that intelligence and usefulness aren't all that matters.

legend.0: Logic is useless for valuing a human life
legend.2: Logic and other considerations matter equally
legend.4: Logic alone fully determines the value of a human life

items.title: Teaching or abuse of power?

state.context: A philosophy teacher runs a thought experiment with his class. He secretly rigged the cards of a student couple. He is having an affair with the female student and believes her boyfriend is beneath her. Within the exercise he forces her to have sex with him and kills students who oppose him.

items.film_note: Petra accuses him of using the exercise to punish her and James.

items.title: Rig a thought experiment to teach a lesson?

state.context: A teacher secretly rigs the role cards in a class exercise. He says it was to confront a privileged student with how ill-prepared he is for the real world.
